summary: Can you give correct change to every customer paying with 5, 10 or 20 bills (each lemonade costs 5)?
mainInsight: Track the number of 5s and 10s. For a 10 you must give a 5; for a 20 prefer giving 10 + 5 (keeping scarce 5s) and otherwise three 5s. Fail if the required bills are not available.

approaches.name: Greedy with bill counts
approaches.summary: Maintain counts of 5 and 10; prefer 10 + 5 for a 20.

promptVariants: How should change for a $20 bill be given?
options: Give a 10 and a 5 if possible because 5s are more versatile
Always give three 5s because they are the smallest bills
Always give two 10s because that uses the fewest bills
Give a 20 back because it matches the bill that was paid
cards.answer: Give a 10 and a 5 if possible because 5s are more versatile
cards.explanation: A 5 can serve both 10 and 20 customers; a 10 can only help a 20, so spend 10s first.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Always give two 10s because that uses th: That equals $20 which is more than $15.

promptVariants: Why is the greedy choice of spending 10s first safe?
What makes 5-dollar bills more valuable than 10s?
cards.answer: Fives are useful for every later customer (10s need one 5; 20s can use one or three 5s), whereas tens are useful only for 20s. So using a ten whenever possible never leaves you worse off.
cards.explanation: An exchange argument shows no alternative is better.

promptVariants: Why are the negative-count checks at the end of each iteration enough to detect failure?
cards.answer: The code spends the required bills even if they do not exist and then fails when a count goes negative - equivalent to failing when a needed bill was missing. For a 20, either one 10 and one 5 (preferred) or three 5s are handed out as change.
cards.explanation: Checking before subtracting is arguably clearer.

options: No: the first 20 uses the 10 and a 5; the last 20 is stuck
Yes: every 20 can be paid back with three 5s each time
Yes: each 20 needs only one 10 as change, in every case
Only if the 10 is kept back for a later customer to use
cards.answer: No: the first 20 uses the 10 and a 5; the last 20 is stuck
cards.explanation: After 5,5 you hold two 5s; the 10 leaves one 5 and one 10; the first 20 uses the 10 and the 5 (change 15); the last 20 then finds no bills at all.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Yes: every 20 can be paid back with thre: Only one 5 remains when the first 20 arrives; three 5s are not available.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Yes: each 20 needs only one 10 as change: A 20 needs change of 15, so one 10 is not enough.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Only if the 10 is kept back for a later: Serving customers in order does not allow choosing to keep the 10.
